cards.text: Jacob, also called Israel, just found out his son Joseph is alive and ruling over all of Egypt (Genesis 45:26-28). So Israel sets out with all that he has, and he stops at a place called Beersheba. Before he goes one step farther, friend, he does something first.

cards.question: Jacob is on his way to Egypt and stops at Beersheba. What does he do there?

answers.text: He digs a new well for water
He buys grain for the long trip

cards.text: That night God speaks to Israel in a vision: "Jacob, Jacob!" When somebody says MY name twice like that, I drop whatever dough I'm holding, and Jacob answers that he's right here.
God says, "I am God," the God of Jacob's father, and Jacob doesn't need to be afraid to go down to Egypt. New country, everything he owns packed up, and God says: don't be afraid.

cards.question: God tells Jacob that down in Egypt, He will make him into a great ___.
True or false: God tells Jacob He will go down to Egypt with him.
God also tells Jacob what He will surely do once they're in Egypt. What is it?

cards.text: Then God adds one more promise, and it's a tender one: "And Joseph's own hands will close your eyes."

cards.question: God tells Jacob that Joseph's own hands will close his eyes. What is that promise about?

answers.text: Joseph will be with him when he dies
Joseph will heal his tired old eyes
Joseph will keep Egypt from his sight

cards.text: So Jacob leaves Beersheba, and his sons carry him in the wagons Pharaoh, king of Egypt, sent for him. Jacob gets moved in the king's own wagons, and when I got moved, I got carried across the kitchen and slid into a DRAWER.

cards.question: Jacob's family heads for Egypt. True or false: they leave their livestock behind in Canaan.

cards.text: Then comes the list of everyone who went: Jacob's sons and their sons, family by family, plus Joseph's two sons born in Egypt, Manasseh and Ephraim. Seventy in all. Friend, I had six cookie cutters on one counter and thought THAT was a crowd.
No map app back then. So Jacob sends one of his sons ahead to Joseph to get directions to Goshen.

cards.question: Jacob sends ___ ahead to Joseph to get directions to Goshen.

cards.text: The family arrives in Goshen, and Joseph gets his chariot ready and goes out to meet his father Israel. No waiting by the window for THIS man.

cards.question: True or false: When Joseph meets his father, he stays up in his chariot and greets him from there.
Joseph is holding his father Israel and weeping. Israel tells him, "Finally I can die." Why does Israel say that?

answers.text: He has seen Joseph is still alive
He is too worn out to go on
He knows Canaan is lost for good

cards.text: Now Joseph's got a plan. He tells the family he'll go tell Pharaoh they've come from Canaan, and that the men are shepherds with their flocks and herds.
Then he gets them ready for Pharaoh's big question: "What is your occupation?" Friend, Joseph is coaching his brothers like it's a JOB INTERVIEW.

cards.question: Joseph tells his brothers to say they've raised livestock ever since their ___, both they and their fathers.
Joseph gives a reason that telling Pharaoh they raise livestock will get them Goshen. What is it?

cards.text: So Joseph tells Pharaoh his father and brothers are in Goshen with everything they own. Then he picks five of his brothers to meet the king, and I bet the other six were just fine sitting that one out.

cards.question: Pharaoh asks Joseph's brothers what their occupation is. True or false: they tell him they're shepherds, like their fathers.
The brothers tell Pharaoh the famine in Canaan is severe and there's no pasture for their flocks. What do they ask him?

answers.text: To let them settle in Goshen
To let them buy grain and leave
To let them graze by the Nile

cards.text: Pharaoh answers, but he says it to Joseph. Moment of truth for a family of shepherds.

cards.question: True or false: Pharaoh tells Joseph to settle his family in the poorest part of the land.
Pharaoh adds an offer: if Joseph knows any talented men among his brothers, put them in charge of Pharaoh's own ___.

cards.text: Then Joseph brings in his father Jacob and presents him before Pharaoh. A shepherd from Canaan, face to face with the king of Egypt.

cards.question: Jacob is standing before Pharaoh, king of Egypt. What does Jacob do?

cards.text: Pharaoh has a question for him: "How many years have you lived?"

cards.question: Jacob tells Pharaoh that his travels have lasted ___ years.
Jacob tells Pharaoh his years haven't matched the years of his fathers' travels. How does he describe his own years?

cards.text: Then Jacob blesses Pharaoh one more time and leaves. TWO blessings in one visit, and I bet the king of Egypt thought he was the one handing out favors.
So Joseph settles his father and brothers in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

cards.question: Joseph's family now has property in Egypt. What else does Joseph provide for his father's whole household?

cards.text: Jacob's whole family, under Joseph's care in Egypt. Keep that apron on, friend, because this family's story is a long way from finished.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "Finally I can die.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke and the Bible fact are joined in one sentence: "I drop whatever dough I'm holding, and Jacob answers that he's right here." This reads as if Papa Dorin's dough and Jacob's reply are one action. Jacob's answer should be its own sentence, apart from the comparison.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says Israel "sets out with all that he has" (46:1). That setup rules out the idea that the family leaves its livestock behind, so the true or false question answers itself.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The summary says the list is "Jacob's sons and their sons" and then "Seventy in all," which makes the seventy sound all male. The text names daughters and granddaughters (46:7), Dinah (46:15) and Serah (46:17). Genesis 46:7 is also not cited by any card: card 11 cites 46:6 and this card starts at 46:8. The card should include the daughters and cite Genesis 46:7-27.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This blank asks the baker to guess the exact wording of Joseph's scripted line ("ever since our youth"), which the baker hasn't seen. It tests the wording of the line, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The first sentence, "Jacob's whole family, under Joseph's care in Egypt," repeats 47:12, which card 18 already asked about. Because the last verse was asked on a choice card, this card should be only the story-isn't-over line.
